name: ripgrep
summary: Exact symbol and text search across tracked trees.
why: Fast, ignore-aware, and sufficient for targeted context. `eng impact` uses it for reference discovery.

name: git grep
summary: Search tracked files without extra tooling.
why: Portable fallback when ripgrep is unavailable; matches the exact revision in Git.

name: Language servers
summary: Compiler-backed definitions, references and diagnostics.
why: The most reliable symbol lookup when the language server is configured. Use it before text search for ambiguous symbols.

name: Cargo metadata
summary: Build graph, package names and targets without reading the tree.
why: The authoritative Rust workspace graph; safer than directory guesses.

name: ast-grep
summary: Structural search and rewrite across many languages.
why: Useful when text search cannot distinguish a definition from a call site. Not adopted until false negatives are measured on real changes.

name: tree-sitter
summary: Incremental parsing for structural indexes.
why: A foundation for symbol extraction, but adds grammars and build surface. Current impact analysis is explicitly textual.

name: SCIP / LSIF
summary: Persistent code-intelligence indexes for large repositories.
why: Would improve cross-repository navigation; not justified until a repository's text search is measurably insufficient.

name: cargo test / nextest
summary: Rust unit, integration and doc tests.
why: Native, deterministic and already the merge condition in Rust repositories.

name: pytest
summary: Python unit and integration tests.
why: Native framework with fixtures and parametrization; used only when the repository declares it.

name: node:test / Vitest
summary: JavaScript and TypeScript tests.
why: Prefer the framework already declared by the repository; do not add a second runner.

name: swift test
summary: Swift package tests on macOS and Linux.
why: Native SwiftPM test runner; required for Swift packages.

name: Gradle test
summary: JVM and Android unit/instrumentation tests.
why: Authoritative for Gradle projects; instrumentation tests need a device or emulator.

name: Property-based testing
summary: Generate inputs from invariants instead of enumerating examples.
why: High value for parsers, math kernels and state machines. Add per repository with a shrinking corpus and a deterministic seed.

name: Fuzzing
summary: Coverage-guided input exploration for parsers and binary formats.
why: Needed for hostile input surfaces. Requires a corpus, a crash triage process and a time budget; not a default fast check.

name: Mutation testing
summary: Test the tests by mutating production code.
why: Useful evidence that a test suite detects faults; expensive and language-specific, so run it on critical modules rather than every commit.

name: Golden and snapshot tests
summary: Freeze serialized output, CLI text, rendering and formats.
why: Strong contract evidence when the golden files are reviewed and regenerated deliberately, never to make a red test green.

name: Contract and differential tests
summary: Old/new fixtures and reference implementations for compatibility.
why: Required for public APIs, schemas, persistence and protocols. A contract claim without a fixture is an opinion.

name: gitleaks
summary: Secret scanning for tracked files and history.
why: High-signal maintained rules. The kit scans a hard-linked tracked tree, so build output is never scanned.

name: Semgrep CE
summary: Language-aware SAST with a small, tested rule set.
why: Runs locally and in CI, supports custom rules and fixtures. Eight baseline rules cover command injection, TLS, YAML, pickle and execSync.

name: OSV-Scanner
summary: Dependency vulnerabilities from lockfiles.
why: Uses OSV data, requires no account and works with Cargo.lock and other ecosystems. Findings are never suppressed to make a gate green.

name: actionlint
summary: GitHub Actions syntax, expression and shell checks.
why: Catches workflow mistakes before merge and works on every workflow file.

name: zizmor
summary: Security audit for GitHub Actions workflows.
why: Finds template injection, credential persistence and unpinned actions. The platform and kit run it as a gate.

name: CodeQL
summary: Deep dataflow and semantic code analysis.
why: Strong for scheduled deep analysis, but heavier and GitHub-hosted. Semgrep remains the fast local gate; add CodeQL where its dataflow adds measured value.

name: Trivy / Grype / Syft
summary: Image, filesystem, SBOM and vulnerability scanning.
why: Adopt when a release produces container images or archives. The current pilot has no such artifact.

name: Cosign
summary: Sign and verify release artifacts and attestations.
why: Only useful once there is an artifact and a signing policy. `release-check` can verify a supplied signature; it does not create keys or sign.

name: Git worktrees
summary: One checkout and branch per independent unit.
why: Native isolation with no extra service. The eng CLI records ownership and a concurrency cap.

name: eng CLI
summary: Detect, impact, verify, guard, security, worktrees and evidence.
why: A dependency-free control plane that gives humans, agents and CI the same answers.

name: GitHub Actions
summary: Shared, immutable quality gates and evidence artifacts.
why: The existing CI system. Add a verify step to it; do not replace working pipelines. Pin every action to a commit SHA.

name: Containers
summary: Ephemeral, reproducible execution where native setup is insufficient.
why: Useful for cross-platform builds and hostile fixtures. Do not add a container runtime when a local process is adequate.

name: sccache / R2
summary: Content-addressed build caching across runners.
why: High value for large Rust workspaces. Requires a private bucket and credentials; never put them in the repository.

name: Evidence records
summary: Hash-chained JSON for every verification run.
why: The audit unit. Records commands, exit codes, durations, output hashes, Git state and scanner versions; skipped is never pass.

name: CI artifacts
summary: Retain evidence outside the agent's context.
why: CI uploads `.agents/evidence/` even when the gate fails, so a reviewer can inspect the failing log after the runner is gone.

name: OpenTelemetry
summary: Traces, metrics and logs across agents and services.
why: Adopt when there is a collector and a consumer for the data. Evidence JSON is the current audit unit.

name: Agent evaluation harness
summary: Scored tasks in isolated worktrees.
why: Measures pass rate, duration and diff size for any agent command. The stub validates the harness; a no-op agent must score zero.

name: AGENTS.md
summary: The repository's authoritative policy and map.
why: One place for commands, invariants, compatibility, security and evidence rules. Skills do not duplicate it.

name: Agent Skills
summary: Ten task-specific entrypoints with workflows and completion criteria.
why: Load one skill for the task instead of injecting every instruction into every context.

name: ADRs and architecture docs
summary: Durable decisions linked to source and tests.
why: Prevents stale chat summaries from overriding current code. Invalidate docs when the code they describe changes.

name: OpenCode
summary: Agent executor with skills, tools and sessions.
why: Reads AGENTS.md and `.opencode/skills`; the installer links the canonical `.agents/skills` there.

name: Codex CLI
summary: Agent executor and AGENTS.md reader.
why: Discovers repository policy through AGENTS.md; the CLI remains the same portable entrypoint.

name: Claude Code
summary: Agent executor with project skills.
why: Reads `.claude/skills`; the installer links the canonical skill directory there.

name: Autobot
summary: Local-first agent with threads, approvals and receipts.
why: The control-plane target: one worktree per thread, durable approvals, signed gateway receipts. Not the default executor for this kit.

name: Invincible gateway
summary: Model gateway with policy, redaction, receipts and audit.
why: The agent should receive a gateway token, not provider keys. Keep it loopback/private and inject credentials at runtime.

name: LiteLLM
summary: Self-hosted model routing and budgets.
why: Centralizes provider keys and model policy. Requires the platform environment and budget configuration.

name: GitHub
summary: Issues, PRs, CI runs, artifacts and checks.
why: The shared collaboration and enforcement surface. Use least-privilege tokens; never commit them.

name: Plane
summary: Work items, projects and delivery tracking.
why: Use when the repository's policy requires the work item to track the change. It does not authorize code changes.

name: pen.dev / Pencil
summary: Design files and rendered UI artifacts.
why: Use for UI design work when the task is visual. It does not replace code, tests or accessibility review.
